query: Why are overtime pay and bonuses included in Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) assessment?
reference_answer: Basic salary, overtime pay, and bonuses are part of a worker’s total income that will help support the worker and his or her family. Given that the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) is intended to supplement the income of lower-wage workers, it is most useful to assess the total income in determining one’s eligibility for WIS.
context:
[Document 1]
Basic salary, overtime pay, and bonuses are part of a worker’s total income that will help support the worker and his or her family. Given that the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) is intended to supplement the income of lower-wage workers, it is most useful to assess the total income in determining one’s eligibility for WIS.

[Document 2]
Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) is based on your net trade income earned in the work year and does not include previous year's losses.

[Document 3]
For the purpose of Workfare Income Supplement (WIS), staff on study/medical/maternity leave will be considered as employees if you are still receiving a salary and CPF contributions from your employers.

[Document 4]
All types of properties e.g. Housing & Development Board flat, private property and non-residential property, are taken into account in determining the eligibility for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme.

[Document 5]
The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme is only for Singaporean lower-wage workers.If you require financial assistance, please contact theComCarehotline at 1800-222-0000, or emailAsk_SSO@msf.gov.sg.
answer: Overtime pay and bonuses are included in the WIS assessment because they contribute to a worker's total income, which helps determine eligibility. The WIS aims to supplement the income of lower-wage workers, so assessing total income provides a fair basis for eligibility [Document 1]. However, WIS focuses on net trade income earned during the current work year, excluding previous years' losses [Document 2].
